Hi Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and a proposed path forward focused on the long-context evaluation you asked about.

Call recap (5 min):
- Primary goal: verify model fidelity when ingesting entire visit notes + supporting documents (~12–18k tokens typical, peak ~28k).
- Key risk: truncation leading to missing context (especially medication history & problem lists) and downstream summarization drift.
- Success metric: extractive fidelity (recall of key fields) + summarization fidelity (ROUGE / human pass-rate on clinical-critical excerpts).

Proposed evaluation plan (high level):
1) Data sample & sandbox access (you provide 50 de-identified notes + 10 long threads; we’ll sign a small DPA + NDA if needed).
2) Run 3 candidate model profiles across your workload:
   - redwood-medium-32k (high-context, recommended baseline)
   - llama3-70b-q4f (cost-efficient large-window option)
   - redwood-quant-16k + prefix-caching (lower cost path with chunking)
3) Benchmarks: automated truncation report, prompt-level fidelity scoring, and a small human review panel for edge cases.
4) Deliverables: evaluation report, prompt set (CSV), recommended rollout config (batching, caching, quant), and a mutual action plan (MAP).

Recommended immediate next steps:
- If you’re comfortable, please share the de-identified sample (SFTP or Drive link) and confirm the procurement contact for a pilot statement of work.
- I’ve attached a starter prompt set and a draft MAP that outlines a 4–6 week pilot.

Thanks Aditya — technical notes below for the eval. I’ll prepare the prompt CSV as an attachment and a short runbook.

Model recommendations (tradeoffs):
- redwood-medium-32k (baseline): expected best fidelity for long contiguous context; minimal truncation; slightly higher per-token cost but lower human-review overhead.
- llama3-70b-q4f (large-window, quantized): good tradeoff for large windows if you can tolerate occasional factuality degradation on rare edge spans. Good for throughput.
- redwood-quant-16k + prefix-caching: lowest cost; use prefix/KV caching for patient demographics and static sections to avoid repeated tokenization of identical headers.

Prompting & truncation guidance:
- Prefer prefixing (patient demographics + critical problem list) and then streaming the remainder. Where context > model window, use chunk+summary pipeline (summary-first / overlap windows of ~2k tokens) to preserve cross-chunk references.
- For extractive fidelity tests, we’ll run a targeted recall suite (entity extraction + section-level checks).

Expected cost ballpark (pilot estimates):
- redwood-medium-32k: $0.03–0.06 per 1k input tokens (higher due to larger window and compute), ~ $2.0k–$4.0k total for pilot sample set.
- llama3-70b-q4f: $0.015–0.035 per 1k input tokens, ~ $900–$2.1k total.
- redwood-quant-16k: $0.008–0.018 per 1k input tokens, ~ $480–$1.1k total.
(These are rough; Steph, please finalize pricing for external.)

Attachments: [Attachment: eunoia_eval_prompts_v1.csv (CSV, 12KB)]
Links: short internal runbook — https://redwood.ai/evals/benchmarks/long-context-2026

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: summarization drift when key events are split across chunks — Mitigation: overlap windows + targeted human verification on flagged cases.
- Risk: PII leakage in logs — Mitigation: enable redaction hooks, disable training ingestion, and provide an audit log of requests. We have SOC2 evidence we can share; Steph can attach the compliance pack.

I’ll package a technical checklist (SFTP steps, de-id template, sample ingestion manifest) and send after the MAP is finalized.

— Neha
